judged_text: createEvent resolves calendarId from only the FIRST entry of event.destinationCalendar (the organizer's) regardless of which host's credential is executing, so the per-destination routing added in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents hands a member host's Lark credential the organizer's calendar id. Collective bookings with multiple Lark hosts fail on every non-first host (Lark rejects writing to a calendar the member's token cannot access), so those hosts' calendars never receive the event — the exact multi-host case this PR claims to fix.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination/credential, but it passes the *same* `event` object each time (does not narrow `event.destinationCalendar` to the current destination). Meanwhile multiple calendar services (e.g. `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, and `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`) resolve the calendarId from only the first entry: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`. So when executing createEvent for a non-first host’s credential, the service will still use the organizer/first destination’s externalId, which can be unauthorized for that credential (e.g., Lark token). GoogleCalendarService was updated to select by `credentialId`, but Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService were not, making multi-host per-destination routing incorrect for those integrations.
